scope: ESP32-P4 controller-level register probe; not real-hardware validation

i2c.bmi270_status: PARTIAL: address responds; UIFlow2 boot clears the preloaded CHIP_ID to 0. An explicit main.py write of 0x24 succeeds, so the native controller and register device are working. A real BMI270 reset/init state machine and dynamic samples remain required.

charger.status: PARTIAL: PI4IOE CHG_STAT/CHG_EN register path and Power.isCharging decode pass for both charging (0x00) and discharging (0x40); IP2326 analog current/termination behavior and hot state injection remain absent

rtc_api.status: PARTIAL: direct machine.I2C write/read reaches RX8130 registers; progression and dynamic host time injection remain absent. machine.RTC only changes the P4 system clock and is not counted as external RTC evidence

notes: This validates the actual P4 I2C controller and UIFlow2 machine.I2C path.
The esp-emu --i2c-dev backend is a writable register file, not a dynamic chip model.
PI4IOE2 CHG_STAT is active-low; the earlier 0x40 observation correctly decoded as not charging.
The diagnostic probe confirms CHIP_ID register zero can store 0x24 after boot; the preload is overwritten before main.py by the UIFlow2 boot board path.
Dynamic values, GPIO side effects and interrupt injection remain partial.
The final framebuffer/touch run used native riscv64-elf-gdb; Docker was not on the critical path.
